title: Burst Of Privileged Group Membership Changes By One Subject
detection_hypothesis: If an adversary consolidates privileges after obtaining administrative access, one subject will add several members to privileged groups in a short burst.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.SubjectUserName: Account that performed the audited action.
field_semantics.TargetUserName: Account or group that was the object of the audited action.

collection_prerequisites: Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
ingestion_differences: Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
false_positive_strategy: Benign bursts correspond to a change ticket and are performed by a known administrator. Tune by requiring a change record and by excluding the migration tooling account only during the migration project.
tuning_guidance: Prefer time-bounded suppression during migrations over permanent exclusion of administrator accounts.
test_strategy: Positive sequences add four or more members within the window. Negative sequences stay under the threshold, spread across subjects, and exceed the window.
